plain_english: Now the fitting cluster of mantras is explained in order, for the accomplishment of those not yet risen to reflection.
sanskrit_cite: atha yathocitamantrakadambakaṃ trikakulakramayogi nirūpyate tāvadvimarśānārūḍhadhiyāṃ tātsiddhaye kramāt

plain_english: Indeed those awakened mantras, whose nature is reflection alone, are endowed with agency from the freedom of the free consciousness-light.
sanskrit_cite: pratibuddhā hi te mantrā vimarśaikasvabhāvakāḥ svatantrasyaiva ciddhāmnaḥ svātantryāt kartṛtāmayāḥ

plain_english: The mantras that enter the teacher, from established identity, make him free, and the instruments too attain agency.
sanskrit_cite: yamāviśanti cācāryaṃ taṃ tādātmyanirūḍhitaḥ svatantrīkurvate yānti karaṇānyapi kartṛtām

plain_english: In the support power, earth and so forth, they say the ordered four-letter set is hrim, kshlam, kshvim, vam, ksham.
sanskrit_cite: ādhāraśaktau hrīṃ pṛthvīprabhṛtau tu catuṣṭaye kṣlāṃ kṣvīṃ vaṃ kṣamiti prāhuḥ kramādvarṇacatuṣṭayam

plain_english: Ham in the channel, yam, ram, lam, vam in the duty fourfold, and rim, rrim, lim, llim in the fourfold, arise in reverse order.
sanskrit_cite: haṃ nāle yaṃ tathā raṃ laṃ vaṃ dharmādicatuṣṭaye ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ ḷḷṃ catuṣke ca viparītakramādbhavet

plain_english: Om, aum, this threefold in knowledge, maya, and kala; anusvara and visarga belong to knowledge, lord, and supreme principle.
sanskrit_cite: oṃ auṃ hastrayamityetadvidyāmāyākalātraye anusvāravisargau ca vidyeśeśvaratattvayoḥ

plain_english: The letters from ka to bha are in the filaments; prana with eight vowels and bindu is in the eight petals; one's own name is illumined.
sanskrit_cite: kādibhāntāḥ kesareṣu prāṇo@ṣṭasvarasaṃyutaḥ sabinduko daleṣvaṣṭasvatha svaṃ nāma dīpitam

plain_english: For the nine powers, sha-sha-sa with bindu are in three circles; kshmam is in preta, and jram is assigned to trident peaks.
sanskrit_cite: śaktīnāṃ navakasya syācchaṣasā maṇḍalatraye sabindukāḥ kṣmaṃ prete jraṃ śūlaśṛṅgeṣu kalpayet

plain_english: In separate seat worship these mantras are remembered in order; in brief worship, the first to last seed syllable is used.
sanskrit_cite: pṛthagāsanapūjāyāṃ kramānmantrā ime smṛtāḥ saṃkṣepapūjane tu prāgādyamantyaṃ ca bījakam

plain_english: Taking from support power to trident peak, one should worship with fire, air, earth, water, sixth vowel, and bindu.
sanskrit_cite: ādāyādhāraśaktyādiśūlaśṛṅgāntamarcayet agnimārutapṛthvyambusaṣaṣṭhasvarabindukam

plain_english: The rati crest mantra of this has a face limb with short and long vowels: fire, prana, fire-destruction, time, indra, water, wind.
sanskrit_cite: ratiśekharamantro@sya vaktrāṅgaṃ hrasvadīrghakaiḥ agniprāṇāgnisaṃhārakālendrāmbusamīraṇāḥ

plain_english: With sixth vowel, bindu, moon, and so forth, the nine self's pervasion through bindu, nada, and so on is held in the triadic head doctrine.
sanskrit_cite: saṣaṣṭhasvarabirndvadhacandrādyāḥ syurnavātmanaḥ bindunādādikā vyāptiḥ śrīmattraiśirase mate

plain_english: The procedure of throwing over, overcoming, awakening and establishing consciousness is thus named: that consciousness, that attainment.
sanskrit_cite: kṣepākrānticidudbodhadīpanasthāpanānyatha tatsaṃvittistadāpattiriti saṃjñābhiśabditā

plain_english: Such is the great pervasion, proclaimed as embodied here; transformation and its dissolution are called salutation.
sanskrit_cite: etāvatī mahāvyāptirmūrtitvenātra kīrtitā pariṇāmastallayaśca namaskāraḥ sa ucyate

plain_english: The three-syllable mantra, joined below with six long vowels, yields the six limbs beginning with the Heart; construct its faces likewise.
sanskrit_cite: eṣa tryarṇojjhito@dhastāddīrghaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ svarairyutaḥ ṣaḍaṅgāni hṛdādīni vaktrāṇyasya ca kalpayet

plain_english: With destruction-sound seeds blazing and bindu-adorned, with jha as the breath of withdrawal, and sa with sixth vowel and drop.
sanskrit_cite: kṣayaravalabījaistu dīptairbinduvibhūṣitaiḥ jhakārasaṃhṛtiprāṇāḥ saṣaṣṭhasvarabindukāḥ

plain_english: This is the abode of Bhairava adorned with half-moon and the rest; the matrka and malini mantras were proclaimed before.
sanskrit_cite: eṣa bhairavasadmāvaścandrārdhādivibhūṣitaḥ mātṛkāmālinīmantrau prāgeva samudāhṛtau

plain_english: Then om, the name in fourth-case ending, obeisance thus in order; among Ganesha and the rest the seed is mantra where none is declared.
sanskrit_cite: oṃkāro@tha caturthyantā saṃjñā natiriti kramāt gaṇeśādiṣu mantraḥ syādbījaṃ yeṣu na coditam

plain_english: The name's first letter illumined with a, bindu and moon is the seed of all seeds, joined with fourteen and sixty.
sanskrit_cite: nāmādyakṣaramākārabinducandrādidīpitam sarveṣāmeva bījānāṃ taccaturdaśaṣaṣṭhayuk

plain_english: Of the triad beginning with the invoked Ghora, seeds arise in order: visarga-bearing maya, hum, and ha with visarga.
sanskrit_cite: āmantritānyaghoryāditritayasya kramoditaiḥ bījairvisargiṇī māyā huṃ hakāro visargavān

plain_english: Again three invocations of the three goddesses in order; in the second word the ka-form with e-sound is recorded here.
sanskrit_cite: punardevītrayasyāpi kramādāmantraṇatrayam dvitīyasminpade@kāra ekārasyeha ca smṛtaḥ

plain_english: Then the two-power mantra with its final letter omitted; both fire letters joined with five vowels, the two distant ones separate.
sanskrit_cite: tataḥ śaktidvayāmantro luptaṃ tatrāntyamakṣaram he@gnivarṇāvubhau pañcasvarayuktau parau pṛthak

plain_english: The astra endowed with a joins hum, ha and the visarga-bearer; the arrow again with Tara, exceeding by two half-syllables of vasu-fire letters.
sanskrit_cite: akārayuktāvastraṃ huṃ ha visargī punaḥ śaraḥ tāreṇa saha vasvagnivarṇārdhārṇadvayādhikā

plain_english: This is the vidya of the supreme-inferior goddess in the Trika teaching, a verse of five-six-five-veda-eye-fire-eye letters.
sanskrit_cite: eṣā parāparādevyā vidyā śrītrikaśāsane pañcaṣaṭpañcavedākṣivahninetrākṣaraṃ padam

plain_english: In the seven beginning with Aghora there is a remainder, each letter associated, in Siddhayogishvari-mata.
sanskrit_cite: aghoryādau saptake syāt pivanyāḥ pariśiṣṭakam pratyekavarṇago@pyuktaḥ siddhayogīśvarīmate

plain_english: The arrangement of the deity circle is not stained due to multiplicity; Maya is visargini, and the mantra is paratmaka with hum and phat.
sanskrit_cite: devatācakravinyāsaḥ sa bahutvānna lipyate māyā visargiṇī huṃ phaṭ ceti mantro@parātmakaḥ

plain_english: The jiva is the pervasion of para with many divisions, stated in Trishira-shastra by Maheshin.
sanskrit_cite: parāyāstūktasadvyāptirjīvaḥ sahacaturdaśaḥ sānekabhedā triśiraḥśāstre proktā maheśinā

plain_english: Though different in nature and entangled in many constructions, here jiva resides in prana, or prana resides in jiva.
sanskrit_cite: svarūpato vibhinnāpi racanānekasaṅkulā jīvaḥ prāṇastha evātra prāṇo vā jīvasaṃsthitaḥ

plain_english: By the relation of support and supported and inseparable yoga, hamsa and amrita in the middle are divided by Kalarudra.
sanskrit_cite: ādhārādheyabhāvena avinābhāvayogataḥ haṃsaṃ cāmṛtamadhyasthaṃ kālarudravibheditam

plain_english: Joined to Bhuvaneshas head with two anangas, brighter than bright, arranged in six chakras, it is to be known.
sanskrit_cite: bhuvaneśaśiroyuktamanaṅgadvayayojitam dīptāddīptataraṃ jñeyaṃ ṣaṭcakrakramayojitam

plain_english: Prana in staff posture is united with secret shakti desire; this supreme is spoken as vacika from the nature of great knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: prāṇaṃ daṇḍāsanasthaṃ tu guhyaśaktīcchayā yutam pareyaṃ vācikoddiṣṭā mahājñānasvarūpataḥ

plain_english: This clear Bhairava heart knowledge is the one-syllable supreme nectar, alone in space, or with Savitri.
sanskrit_cite: sphuṭaṃ bhairavahṛjjñānamidaṃ tvekākṣaraṃ param amṛtaṃ kevalaṃ khasthaṃ yadvā sāvitrikāyutam

plain_english: The supreme heart of para, endowed with two voids, well known in paired sacrifice, is to be done by knowers of tattva.
sanskrit_cite: śūnyadvayasamopetaṃ parāyā hṛdayaṃ param yugmayāge prasiddhaṃ tu kartavyaṃ tattvavedibhiḥ

plain_english: Other one-syllable mantras are hidden, more hidden by Ekavira rite, and devoid of limbs and family.
sanskrit_cite: anye@pyekākṣarā ye tu ekavīravidhānataḥ guptā guptatarāste tu aṃgābhijanavarjitāḥ

plain_english: They are to be worshipped by siddha leaders, abiding in kula and giving siddhi, through kula rite with subtle knowledge yoga.
sanskrit_cite: yaṣṭavyāḥ sādhakendraistu kulasthāḥ siddhidāyakāḥ kulakramavidhānena sūkṣmavijñānayogataḥ

plain_english: These are to be performed always, O goddess, by woman or man, with sa joined with six longs, limbs and faces.
sanskrit_cite: anuṣṭheyāḥ sadā devi striyā vā puruṣeṇa vā sakāro dīrghaṣaṭkena yukto@ṅgānyānanāni tu

plain_english: That supreme one, joined with five short vowels and kha and accompanied by five om syllables, becomes the five-syllabled mantra, the heart of the vidya limb.
sanskrit_cite: syāt sa eva paraṃ hrasvapañcasvarakhasaṃyutaḥ oṃkāraiḥ pañcabhirmantro vidyāṅgahṛdayaṃ bhavet

plain_english: In amrita and tejomala, om together with svaha becomes the eleven-syllabled brahma head in the tanmalini view.
sanskrit_cite: praṇavaścāmṛte tejomālini svāhayā saha ekādaśākṣaraṃ brahmaśirastanmālinīmate

plain_english: The crest, joined with om and so forth, with hum and phat, is for vajrin and vajradhara, preceded by svaha and om.
sanskrit_cite: vedavedani hūṃ phaṭca praṇavādiyutā śikhā vajriṇe vajradharāya svāhetyoṃkārapūrvakam

plain_english: The eleven-syllabled armor, remembered as purush praised, includes tara, two-tongued, and life with kha sha ra vowels pair.
sanskrit_cite: ekādaśākṣaraṃ varma puruṣṭutamiti smṛtam tāro dvijihvaḥ khaśarasvarayugjīva eva ca

plain_english: This radiant eye, common to all, is remembered; tara, shlim, beast, hum, and phat form that weapon of rasa color.
sanskrit_cite: netrametatprakāśātma sarvasādhāraṇaṃ smṛtam tāraḥ ślīṃ paśu huṃ phat ca tadastraṃ rasavarṇakam

plain_english: With long lara taksha vaya joined with bindu, indra and others have those weapons; short forms belong to vishnu and prajapati.
sanskrit_cite: laraṭakṣavayairdīrghaiḥ samayuktaiḥ sabindukaiḥ indrādayastadastrāṇi hrasvairviṣṇuprajāpatī

plain_english: In memory, by fourth and second short forms in the lotus wheel, the classes nama, svaha, vaushat, hum, vashat, and phat arise.
sanskrit_cite: smṛtau turyadvitīyābhyāṃ hrasvābhyāṃ padmacakrake namaḥ svāhā tathā vauṣaṭ huṃ vaṣaṭ phaṭ ca jātayaḥ

plain_english: In the six limbs in order, those classes are of that nature in rites, in recitation, offering, nourishing, agitating, and pacifying.
sanskrit_cite: aṅgeṣu kramaśaḥ ṣaṭsu karmasvatha tadātmikāḥ jape home tathāpyāye samuccāṭe@tha śāntike

plain_english: In hostile rites, for mantras, the classes from namaskara onward are second, going to eye and six sage groups with bindu.
sanskrit_cite: abhicāre ca mantrāṇāṃ namaskārādijātayaḥ akṣiṣaṇmunivargebhyo dvitīyāḥ saha bindunā

plain_english: By yoni syllable, the seats of mothers, with time drawing, are approved, whether omitted at beginning or end.
sanskrit_cite: yonyarṇena ca mātṝṇāṃ sadmāvaḥ kālakarṣiṇī ādyojjhito vāpyantena varjito vātha saṃmataḥ

plain_english: Life, standing inside the prana fold, with radiance equal to time fire, is very radiant and adorned with the left foot on the head with bindu.
sanskrit_cite: jīvaḥ prāṇapuṭāntaḥsthaḥ kālānalasamadyutiḥ atidīptastu vāmāṃghrirbhūṣito mūrdhni bindunā

plain_english: This form following the right knee, worshipped by all mother groups, grants desired fruit to all living beings.
sanskrit_cite: dakṣajānugataścāyaṃ sarvamātṛgaṇārcitaḥ anena prāṇitāḥ sarve dadate vāñchitaṃ phalam

plain_english: This supreme reality belongs to the mothers and to Bhairava, so the mantra practitioner who desires supreme accomplishment should recite it.
sanskrit_cite: sadbhāvaḥ paramo hyeṣa mātṝṇāṃ bhairavasya ca tasmādenaṃ japenmantrī ya icchetsiddhimuttamām

plain_english: Rudra power entry is always established here, because this supreme power is declared as distinct from another.
sanskrit_cite: rudraśaktisamāveśo nityamatra pratiṣṭhitaḥ yasmādeṣā parā śaktirbhedenānyena kīrtitā

plain_english: This power performs all accomplishments found in tantra, and her limbs and faces arise by prior sound assignment.
sanskrit_cite: yāvatyaḥ siddhayastantre tāḥ sarvāḥ kurute tviyam aṅgavaktrāṇi cāpyasyāḥ prāgvatsvaraniyogataḥ

plain_english: Staff, living being, trident, right finger, breasts, navel, throat, wind, Rudra, and emission with trident are listed as correspondences.
sanskrit_cite: daṇḍo jīvastriśūlaṃ ca dakṣāṅgulyaparastanau nābhikaṇṭhau marudrudrau visargaḥ satriśūlakaḥ

plain_english: This lord of all yogini circles is declared, and awareness arises by her utterance alone.
sanskrit_cite: sarvayoginicakrāṇāmadhipo@yamudāhṛtaḥ asyāpyuccāraṇādeva saṃvittiḥ syātpuroditā

plain_english: The eight-lettered form is called great fierce yoga lord, while the nine-lettered form is the more secret true being, time-drawing.
sanskrit_cite: mahācaṇḍeti tu yogeśvaṛ ityaṣṭavarṇakam navārṇeyaṃ guptatarā sadbhāvaḥ kālakarṣiṇī

plain_english: In the great sacrifice of Shri Damara, a beyond-beyond form is declared, with seed and cutting vowel.
sanskrit_cite: śrīḍāmare mahāyāge parātparataroditā sudhācchedakaṣaṇṭhādyairbījaṃ chedakamasvaram

plain_english: In Malini view, the one-and-half-syllabled night of time is the knife; by repeating it one hundred times, pain arises in the head.
sanskrit_cite: adhyardhārṇā kālarātriḥ kṣurikā mālinīmate śatāvartanayā hyasyā jāyate mūrdhni vedanā

plain_english: Having considered conviction, one should resort to death-conquering meditation; one desiring long life should not recite this.
sanskrit_cite: evaṃ pratyayamālocya mṛtyujiddhyānamāśrayet naināṃ samuccareddevi ya iccheddīrghajīvitam

plain_english: Two staff fires, trident, sky, life, cutting, reed, peak fires with emission, and five items are placed in five locations.
sanskrit_cite: dvirdaṇḍāgnī śūlanabhaḥprāṇāśchettranalau tathā kūṭāgnī savisargāśca pañcāpyete@tha pañcasu

plain_english: Shiva stated in the tantra true-being teaching that the cutting knife joins the supreme.
sanskrit_cite: vyomasviti śivenoktaṃ tantrasadbhāvaśāsane chedinī kṣurikeyaṃ syādyayā yojayate pare

plain_english: One should remember this blazing weapon, joined with bindu, fire, peak, wind, and sixth vowel, from the sole of the foot to the top of the head.
sanskrit_cite: bindvindvanalakūṭāgnimarutṣaṣṭhasvarairyutam āpādatalamūrdhāntaṃ smaredastramidaṃ jvalat

plain_english: Contract the fingers, then stimulate; crossing from knee and other chakras, contract from chakra to chakra.
sanskrit_cite: kuñcanaṃ cāṅgulīnāṃ tu kartavyaṃ codanaṃ tataḥ jānvādiparacakrāntaṃ cakrāccakraṃ tu kuñcayet

plain_english: The secret teaching giving immediate liberation is supreme; now brahma-knowledge is stated, giving immediate conviction.
sanskrit_cite: kathitaṃ sarahasyaṃ tu sadyonirvāṇakaṃ param athocyate brahmavidyā sadyaḥpratyayadāyinī

plain_english: Shiva, Sri Bhutiraja, taught us when death of all beings is imminent.
sanskrit_cite: śivaḥ śrībhūtirājo yāmasmabhyaṃ pratyapādayat sarveṣāmeva bhūtānāṃ maraṇe samupasthite

plain_english: By which, having read and transcended, the soul goes to the stainless; even for a knower with completed duty, when heard, it is.
sanskrit_cite: yayā paṭhitayotkramya jīvo yāti nirañjanam yā jñānino@pi saṃpūrṇakṛtyasyāpi śrutā satī

plain_english: It immediately removes death-pain born from prana severance; hearing it, even one overcome by great delusion gradually attains.
sanskrit_cite: prāṇādicchedajāṃ mṛtyuvyathāṃ sadyo vyapohati yāmākarṇya mahāmohavivaśo@pi kramādgataḥ

plain_english: Awakening, the speaker's presence approaches swiftly by itself; from the supreme state you have come here; eternal you, abandon the body-end.
sanskrit_cite: prabodhaṃ vaktṛsāṃmukhyamabhyeti rabhasātsvayam paramapadāttvamihāgāḥ sanātanastvaṃ jahīhi dehāntam

plain_english: From toe etc, lord, binding; indeed fierce bond; this noble statement first becomes by world-named words.
sanskrit_cite: pādāṅguṣṭhādi vibho nibandhanaṃ bandhanaṃ hyugram āryāvākyamidaṃ pūrvaṃ bhuvanākhyaiḥ padairbhavet

plain_english: At ankle, knee-placed, collarbone-placed binding; likewise at groin abandon the foremost middle city; from heart-lotus you arise.
sanskrit_cite: gulphānte jānugataṃ jatrusthaṃ bandhanaṃ tathā meḍhre jahihi puramagryamadhyaṃ hṛtpadmāttvaṃ samuttiṣṭha

plain_english: By these many words this noble statement is second; Hamsa, Hayagriva, lord, you are supreme Sadashiva, called Jiva.
sanskrit_cite: etāvadbhiḥ padairetadāryāvākyaṃ dvitīyakam haṃsa hayagrīva vibho sadāśivastvaṃ paro@si jīvākhyaḥ

plain_english: Sun-moon-fire-group-drop-body, hahaha, transcend; third noble statement, by previous counts plus one words.
sanskrit_cite: ravisomavahnisaṅghadṛbindudeho hahaha samutkrāma tṛtīyamāryāvākyaṃ prāksaṃkhyairekādhikaiḥ padaiḥ

plain_english: Composed of the hamsa great mantra, eternal you; expecting auspicious and inauspicious; situated in the middle of the mandala; cause of the great bridge of shakti, great meaning.
sanskrit_cite: haṃsamahāmantramayaḥ sanātanastvaṃ śubhāśubhāpekṣī maṇḍalamadhyaniviṣṭaḥ śaktimahāsetukāraṇamahārthaḥ

plain_english: Situated in both lotuses, come to awakening, divine body; this noble statement along with rudra-count words.
sanskrit_cite: kamalobhayaviniviṣṭaḥ prabodhamāyāhi devatādeha āryāvākyamidaṃ sārdhaṃ rudrasaṃkhyapaderitam

plain_english: From ignorance you are bound; awaken and rise, O god.
sanskrit_cite: niḥśvāse tvapaśabdasya sthāne@styupa iti dhvaniḥ ajñānāttvaṃ baddhaḥ prabodhitottiṣṭha devāde

plain_english: This fifth half-verse has seven words; go to the palate-named end, the bronze-struck great gate.
sanskrit_cite: etatpañcamamāryārdhavākyaṃ syātsaptabhiḥ padaiḥ vraja tālusāhvayāntaṃ hyauḍambaraghaṭṭitaṃ mahādvāram

plain_english: Having reached, proceed, ho ho, or to Vamadeva station; this sixth sentence has fourteen words.
sanskrit_cite: prāpya prayāhi haṃho haṃho vā vāmadevapadam āryyāvākyamidaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ syāccaturdaśabhiḥ padaiḥ

plain_english: O lord of knots, supreme self, peaceful one, having reached the great palate hole transcend; O lord of body, quickly go to stainless Shiva station.
sanskrit_cite: granthīśvara paramātman śānta mahātālurandhramāsādya utkrama he deheśvara nirañjanaṃ śivapadaṃ prayāhyāśu

plain_english: The seventh sentence may have fourteen words; the reading in the exhalation teaching says you are wind.
sanskrit_cite: āryāvākyaṃ saptamaṃ syāttaccaturdaśabhiḥ padaiḥ prabhañjanastvamityevaṃ pāṭho niḥśvāsaśāsane

plain_english: Having traversed the middle path, gathered prana and apana, and abandoned merit and demerit, Narayana, go to the peaceful end.
sanskrit_cite: ākramya madhyamārgaṃ prāṇāpānau samāhṛtya dharmādharmau tyaktvā nārāyaṇa yāhi śāntāntam

plain_english: This eighth sentence has nine words: O Brahman, O Vishnu, O Rudra, you are Shiva, you are Vasudeva.
sanskrit_cite: āryāvākyamidaṃ proktamaṣṭamaṃ navabhiḥ padaiḥ he brahman he viṣṇo he rudra śivo@si vāsudevastvam

plain_english: Destroy the eternal clay lump of Agni-Soma, O great space; this sentence is proclaimed counted by worlds.
sanskrit_cite: agnīṣomasanātanamṛtpiṇḍaṃ jahihi he mahākāśa etadbhuvanasaṃkhyātairāryyāvākyaṃ prakīrtitam

plain_english: With self, three lumps, great sheath; three words are situated in exhalation, crown, Uttara and so on.
sanskrit_cite: sanātma tripiṇḍamiti mahākośamiti sthitam padatrayaṃ tu niḥśvāsamukuṭottarakādiṣu

plain_english: Destroy the thumb-sized pure covering, O great subtle; this tenth sentence is said to have six words.
sanskrit_cite: aṅguṣṭhamātramamalamāvaraṇaṃ jahihi he mahāsūkṣma āryyāvākyamidaṃ ṣaḍbhiḥ padairdaśamamucyate

plain_english: Enough, twice subtle; thus in Shri Mukuta Uttara, you are person bound by nature, ego thread, and bonds.
sanskrit_cite: alaṃ dviriti sūkṣmaṃ cetyevaṃ śrīmukuṭottare puruṣastvaṃ prakṛtimayairbaddho@haṅkāratantunā bandhaiḥ

plain_english: Renounce the supreme soul—eternally risen, of non-existence and existence—on the passionate path; this thirteen-word phrase may be the supreme noble speech.
sanskrit_cite: abhavābhava nityodita paramātmaṃstyaja sarāgamadhvānam etattrayodaśapadaṃ syādāryāvākyamuttamam

plain_english: O body of the hrīṃ-hūṃ mantra, come quickly without delay to the end of the body; this may be the noble half-sentence, the twelfth, six-footed, supreme.
sanskrit_cite: hrīṃhūṃmantraśarīramavilambamāśu tvamehi dehāntam āryārdhavākyametatsyād dvādaśaṃ ṣaṭpadaṃ param

plain_english: Abandon this quality-made, own, six-sheathed mass; it may be the thirteenth half-āryā, with seven such words.
sanskrit_cite: tadidaṃ guṇabhūtamayaṃ tyaja sva ṣoṭkośikaṃ piṇḍam syāt trayodaśamāryārdhaṃ padaiḥ saptabhirīdṛśam

plain_english: Do not take the body made of elements; take the eternal great body. This noble half-sentence, in so many words, is the fourteenth.
sanskrit_cite: mā dehaṃ bhūtamayaṃ pragṛhyatāṃ śāśvataṃ mahādeham āryārdhavākyaṃ tāvadbhiḥ padairetaccaturdaśam

plain_english: Go, having pierced this pure, endless circle situated in three ways; but this noble half-verse is fifteen by eight words.
sanskrit_cite: maṇḍalamamalamanantaṃ tridhā sthitaṃ gaccha bhittvaitat āryārdhavākyamaṣṭābhiḥ padaiḥ pañcadaśaṃ tvidam

plain_english: This brahma knowledge with parts may have fifteen clear sentences; its five-syllable form is proclaimed without parts.
sanskrit_cite: sakaleyaṃ brahmavidyā syātpañcadaśabhiḥ sphuṭaiḥ vākyaiḥ pañcākṣaraistvasyā niṣkalā parikīrtyate

plain_english: The reply is recited with its beginning and end joined; it comprises tāra, māyā, vedakala, mother-tāra, and the nine-formed.
sanskrit_cite: prativākyaṃ yayādyantayojitā paripaṭhyate tāro māyā vedakalo mātṛtāro navātmakaḥ

plain_english: Thus, according to proclaimed pervasion, there are five syllables: bindu, prana, nectar, water, and wind endowed with the sixth vowel.
sanskrit_cite: iti pañcākṣarāṇi syuḥ proktavyāptyanusārataḥ binduprāṇāmṛtajalaṃ marutṣaṣṭhasvarānvitam

plain_english: By this, through the seed situated in the utterance of shakti, the bound soul who has performed the initiation rite is obtained; even one who was formerly a slayer of a brahmin becomes purified.
sanskrit_cite: etena śaktyuccārasthabījenālabhyate paśuḥ kṛtadīkṣāvidhiḥ pūrvaṃ brahmaghno@pi viśuddhyati

plain_english: By lightness the balance becomes pure and immediately causes certainty; tara, shamara, lump, and bow are four-lettered.
sanskrit_cite: laghutvena tulāśuddhiḥ sadyaḥpratyayakāriṇī tāraḥ śamarayaiḥ piṇḍo natiśca caturarṇakam

plain_english: Subduing Shakini is the vital point of heart and life; but this is by sixth prana, trikuta, upraised arm, spear-named bindus.
sanskrit_cite: śākinīstobhanaṃ marma hṛdayaṃ jīvitaṃ tvidam ṣaṣṭhaprāṇatrikūṭordhvabāhuśūlākhyabindubhiḥ

plain_english: The heart adorned with anacka, nose, lower face, and moon pieces is called Bhairava and is all-destroying.
sanskrit_cite: anackanāsādhovaktracandrakhaṇḍaiśca maṇḍitam hṛdayaṃ bhairavākhyaṃ tu sarvasaṃhārakārakam

plain_english: Shakinis heated by Bhairava fire in the middle of the fire circle come under control; if this place burns.
sanskrit_cite: agnimaṇḍalamadhyasthabhairavānalatāpitāḥ vaśamāyānti śākinyaḥ sthānametena ceddahet

plain_english: Dismiss them first, otherwise they pierce; with these letters hreem, kleem, vlem, klem adorned with twelve vowels.
sanskrit_cite: visarjayettāḥ prathamamanyathā cchidrayanti tāḥ hrīṃ klīṃ vleṃ kleṃ ebhirvarṇairdvādaśasvarabhūṣitaiḥ

plain_english: The heart named union of loved ones is a joined pair; chant it individually, or with two, or with all; this is the best rule.
sanskrit_cite: priyamelāpanaṃ nāma hṛdayaṃ sampuṭaṃ japet pratyekamathavā dvābhyāṃ sarvairvā vidhiruttamaḥ

plain_english: The balance-union yoga in the Shri Tantra true-being teaching, spoken by Shambhunatha, has been shown by me in order.
sanskrit_cite: tulāmelakayogaḥ śrītantrasadbhāvaśāsane ya uktaḥ śambhunāthena sa mayā darśitaḥ kramāt

plain_english: Now for those without wealth and for devotees truly, the fault of place, time, and so on is not so for those with such resolve.
sanskrit_cite: atha vittavihīnānāṃ prapannānāṃ ca tattvataḥ deśakālādidoṣeṇa na tathādhyavasāyinām

plain_english: Initiation should be done as told, delighted by the Shri lineage, urged by the Hatakesha Patala lord.
sanskrit_cite: prakartavyā yathā dīKṣā śrīsantatyāgamoditā kathyate hāṭakeśānapātālādhipacoditā

plain_english: O Shri Natha, noble lord, this triad indeed: root, support, Varuna, my desire, lordship; this triad is in the heart.
sanskrit_cite: śrīnātha ārya bhagavannetattritayaṃ hi kanda ādhāre varuṇo macchando bhagavatta iti trayamidaṃ hṛdaye

plain_english: The four named groups from dharma are in the throat region, worshipful, beginning with hreem shreem, all endowed with address and ending with foot words.
sanskrit_cite: dharmādivargasaṃjñāścatvāraḥ kaṇṭhadeśagāḥ pūjyāḥ hrīṃśrīṃpūrvāḥ sarve sambodhajuṣaśca pādaśabdāntāḥ

plain_english: At the head base three knowledges are stated; then meditate by mind union, with flowers or joys, or by meditation alone.
sanskrit_cite: mūrdhatale vidyātrayamuktaṃ bhāvyatha mano@bhiyogena kusumairānandairvā bhāvanayā vāpi kevalayā

plain_english: When the truth-knowing guru finds a disciple heart-made for liberation alone, skilled in liberation's sole gift, this is the supreme-upanisad initiation.
sanskrit_cite: guruṇā tattvavidā kila śiṣyo yadi mokṣamātrakṛtahṛdayaḥ mokṣaikadānacaturā dīkṣā seyaṃ paropaniṣaduktā

plain_english: Initiated into this initiation, remembering this threefold vidya in the heart, without outer worship and the rest, he reaches the supreme abode at body's end.
sanskrit_cite: etaddīkṣādīkṣita etadvidyātrayaṃ smaran hṛdaye bāhyārcādi vinaiva hi vrajati paraṃ dhāma dehānte

plain_english: Om and maya with bindu: make three letters from the start into five addressed words ending with the fire-god's beloved.
sanskrit_cite: praṇavo māyā bindurvarṇatrayamāditaḥ kuryāt padapañcakasya saṃbodhanayuktasyāgnidayitānte

plain_english: The accomplished-accomplishing power in sound-brahman form, joined with the word of every bond, cuts.
sanskrit_cite: siddhasādhani tatpūrvaṃ śabdabrahmasvarūpiṇi samastabandhaśabdena sahitaṃ ca nikṛntani

plain_english: In awakening, invoked by the mother of Siva's true being, the five-footed verse runs in five-eight and three-eight order.
sanskrit_cite: bodhani śivasadbhāvajananyāmantritaṃ ca tat pañcāṣṭarandhratryaṣṭārṇakrameṇa padapañcakam

plain_english: The sky-five-syllable supreme-brahman vidya gives liberation, auspicious, in supreme desire with bell and thirteen tones.
sanskrit_cite: khapañcārṇā parabrahmavidyeyaṃ mokṣadā śivā anuttarecche ghāntaśca satrayodaśasusvaraḥ

plain_english: At the three letters' end the four semivowels ending in ta; first-of-class and horse with triangle-bindu joined, from three letters after pa.
sanskrit_cite: asya varṇatrayasyānte tvantaḥsthānāṃ catuṣṭayam vargādyaśvau tryasrabinduyuk pānto@rṇatrayādataḥ

plain_english: The great-golden-sound seven-syllable mantra of the goddess, addressed forgive-thus in three syllables, ending sin.
sanskrit_cite: mahāhāṭakaśabdādyamīśvarītyarṇasaptakam āmantritaṃ kṣamasveti tryarṇaṃ pāpāntakāriṇi

plain_english: The six-syllabled deluding word beginning with the sinful word; then kill, shake off, in twice-twice-ten syllables, such is the word.
sanskrit_cite: ṣaḍarṇaṃ pāpaśabdādivimohanipadaṃ tataḥ pāpaṃ hana dhuna dvirdvirdaśārṇaṃ padamīdṛśam

plain_english: By Rudra-Sakti power the six-letter form ending in fifth case; then the one syllable declared, the visarga-brahman.
sanskrit_cite: pañcamyantaṃ ṣaḍarṇaṃ syādrudraśaktivaśāditi tata ekākṣaraṃ yattadvisargabrahma kīrtitam

plain_english: In union with that act recite: hole-ocean letters, this vidya called initiation-knowledge.
sanskrit_cite: tadanackatakāreṇa sahaikībhāvataḥ paṭhet randhrābdhivarṇā vidyeyaṃ dīkṣāvidyeti kīrtitā

plain_english: Maya-syllable in supreme brahman with four vidyas, three feet; eight syllables then five, named yoga-bearer.
sanskrit_cite: māyārṇañca pare brahme caturvidye padatrayam aṣṭārṇamatha pañcārṇaṃ yogadhāriṇisaṃjñitam

plain_english: A ten-syllabled form ending in e, situated in knowledge and made of three words, is proclaimed as the form of self, inner self, and supreme self.
sanskrit_cite: ātmāntarātmaparamātmarūpaṃ ca padatrayam ekārāntaṃ bodhanasthaṃ daśārṇaṃ parikīrtitam

plain_english: May it be, O beloved of Rudra, that this veda-syllable Rudra-shakti burns my sin; this formula is twelve-syllabled and four-footed.
sanskrit_cite: rudraśaktīti vedārṇaṃ syādrudradayite@tha me pāpaṃ dahadahetyeṣā dvādaśārṇā catuṣpadī

plain_english: O gentle Sadashiva, this convention-removing formula contains a pair and six, brings bindu and arrow, and has four half-syllables.
sanskrit_cite: saumye sadāśive yugmaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ bindviṣusāvahā sārdhavarṇacatuṣkaṃ tadityeṣā samayāpahā

plain_english: This knowledge, counted as half-syllable, kha, and arrow, is the supreme lady; glorious Bhutiraja described this triad of knowledges.
sanskrit_cite: vidyā sārdhārṇakhaśarasaṃkhyā sā pārameśvarī etadvidyātrayaṃ śrīmadbhūtirājo nyarūpayat

plain_english: The glorious Śrīkaṇṭha, who directly worshipped the human body, has power previously stated; the guru should follow it everywhere.
sanskrit_cite: yaḥ sākṣādabhajacchrīmāñśrīkaṇṭho mānuṣīṃ tanum atra vīryaṃ puraivoktaṃ sarvatrānusaredguruḥ

plain_english: According to meaning, seed, entry, and so on, nothing at all exists that was not previously explained.
sanskrit_cite: arthabījapraveśāntaruccārādyanusārataḥ nahi tatkiṃcanāpyasti yatpurā na nirūpitam

plain_english: Repetition is fruitless to us; thus the nature of mantra knowledge and so on has been described.
sanskrit_cite: niṣphalā punaruktistu nāsmabhyaṃ jātu rocate ityevaṃ mantravidyādisvarūpamupavarṇitam
